stem: Which exposure factor directly controls the quantity of x-ray photons produced, and so the exposure reaching the image receptor?
explanation: Milliampere-seconds sets the number of photons produced; doubling the mAs doubles the exposure.

stem: According to the 15% rule, increasing the kilovoltage by 15% will
options: have no effect on receptor exposure
explanation: A 15% increase in kVp doubles the exposure at the receptor, so the mAs can be halved to keep it the same.

stem: A good image is made at 70 kVp and 10 mAs. To use 80 kVp while keeping the same receptor exposure, the mAs should be about
explanation: Going from 70 to about 80 kVp is a 15% increase, which doubles the exposure, so the mAs is halved to 5.

stem: Compared with a nongrid exposure, an 8:1 grid requires the mAs to be multiplied by
explanation: Common grid conversion factors: 5:1 = 2, 6:1 = 3, 8:1 = 4, 12:1 = 5 and 16:1 = 6.

stem: A nongrid exposure uses 5 mAs. If a 12:1 grid is added, the new mAs should be
explanation: The 12:1 grid factor is 5, so 5 mAs × 5 = 25 mAs.

stem: An exposure at 40 in SID uses 10 mAs. If the SID is changed to 80 in, what mAs will keep the same receptor exposure?
explanation: By the exposure maintenance (direct square) formula, doubling the SID needs four times the mAs: 10 × 4 = 40 mAs.

stem: Raising the kVp, with the mAs adjusted to keep receptor exposure the same, produces
explanation: Higher kVp penetrates tissues more evenly and produces more scatter, so there are more shades of gray and contrast is lower.

stem: Which change increases magnification of the part being imaged?
explanation: The farther the part is from the image receptor, the more it is magnified. Short OID and long SID reduce magnification.

stem: Which focal spot setting gives the best recorded detail (spatial resolution)?
options: Either, because focal spot size does not affect detail
The focal spot that allows the shortest SID
explanation: A smaller focal spot produces less geometric unsharpness (penumbra), so detail is better.

stem: Shape distortion (elongation or foreshortening) is caused by
options: misalignment of the tube, part and image receptor
explanation: When the central ray, the part and the receptor are not properly aligned, the part's shape is distorted. Size distortion (magnification) comes from SID and OID.

stem: Because the target is angled, the effective focal spot is smaller than the actual focal spot. This is the
explanation: The line focus principle lets a large area of the target take the heat while a small effective focal spot gives good detail.

stem: Because of the anode heel effect, the thicker part of the anatomy should be placed under the
explanation: Beam intensity is greater on the cathode side, so the thicker part goes toward the cathode to even out the exposure.

stem: Tungsten is used for the target because it has a high melting point and a high atomic number of
explanation: Tungsten (Z = 74) produces x-rays efficiently, and its melting point of 3,410 °C helps it withstand the heat.

stem: Most of the x-rays in the diagnostic beam are produced when incoming electrons
options: eject inner-shell electrons of the target
are slowed and deflected by the nucleus of a target atom
explanation: Bremsstrahlung (braking) radiation is produced when electrons are slowed by the nuclear field; it makes up most of the beam.

stem: Characteristic radiation is produced when
options: an electron is slowed by the nucleus
an inner-shell electron is ejected and an outer-shell electron fills the vacancy
explanation: When an outer-shell electron drops into the inner-shell vacancy, the energy difference is given off as a characteristic x-ray photon.

stem: Electrons are freed from the heated cathode filament by
explanation: Heating the tungsten filament boils off electrons: thermionic emission.

stem: The anode heel effect is most pronounced with
options: a short SID and a large image receptor
a long SID and a small image receptor
explanation: A short SID and a large receptor use more of the beam on the anode side, where the heel absorbs the most, so the difference in intensity is greatest.

stem: The main advantage of a rotating anode is that it
options: spreads the heat over a larger area of the target
explanation: Rotation spreads the heat over the whole focal track, so the tube can take higher exposures.

stem: For single-phase equipment, heat units are calculated as
explanation: Heat units for single-phase equipment equal kVp × mA × seconds; three-phase and high-frequency equipment use a multiplier.

stem: Increasing the grid ratio changes
options: the amount of scatter produced in the patient
the size of the focal spot
the amount of scatter reaching the image receptor
explanation: Grid ratio has no effect on how much scatter the patient produces, but a higher ratio absorbs more of it before it reaches the receptor.

stem: Which transformer raises the voltage to the kilovolt level the x-ray tube needs?
explanation: The step-up transformer raises the voltage to the kilovolts needed to drive electrons across the tube; the step-down transformer supplies the filament.

stem: Which type of generator has the lowest voltage ripple?
explanation: High-frequency generators produce nearly constant voltage, with less than 1% ripple, giving a more efficient beam.

stem: The backup timer of an automatic exposure control (AEC) serves to
explanation: If the AEC fails to end the exposure, the backup timer stops it, protecting the patient and the tube.

stem: In most automatic exposure control systems, the ionization chambers are located
options: between the patient and the image receptor
explanation: The chambers sit just in front of the image receptor and end the exposure when a preset amount of radiation reaches them.

stem: The collimator light field and the actual irradiated area must agree to within
explanation: Collimator and beam alignment must be accurate to within 2% of the SID.

stem: Repeated exposures at the same technique settings must give consistent intensity. This requirement is called
explanation: Reproducibility means the same technique always produces the same output.

stem: The same mAs produced with different mA stations and matching exposure times must give the same intensity. This is
explanation: Linearity means a given mAs gives the same output whichever mA station is used.

stem: Which test tool is used to measure the size of the focal spot?
explanation: A star pattern (or slit or pinhole camera) shows the effective focal spot size.

stem: On single-phase equipment, a spinning top test checks the accuracy of the
explanation: The number of dots imaged by the spinning top shows whether the timer gives the exposure time selected.

stem: A wire mesh test is used to evaluate
explanation: Areas of blurring in the image of the wire mesh show poor contact between the screen and the film.

stem: A focused grid placed upside down produces
options: severe grid cutoff toward the edges
explanation: The lead strips then slant away from the divergent beam, absorbing it toward the edges while the center is exposed.

stem: Grid ratio is the
options: number of lead strips per inch
distance at which the grid is focused
height of the lead strips divided by the distance between them
explanation: Grid ratio is strip height divided by interspace width; higher ratios remove more scatter.

stem: Compared with a 6:1 grid, a 12:1 grid
options: removes more scatter but needs more exposure
removes less scatter and needs less exposure
removes the same scatter with less exposure
explanation: A higher grid ratio cleans up more scatter, but the mAs must rise to compensate, which raises patient dose.

stem: In computed radiography (CR), the photostimulable phosphor imaging plate is usually made of
explanation: Barium fluorohalide stores the latent image, which is released as light when the plate is scanned by a laser.

stem: A direct-capture flat-panel detector changes x-ray photons straight into electric charge using
explanation: Amorphous selenium converts x-rays directly to charge; indirect systems first convert x-rays to light in a scintillator.

stem: An indirect-capture flat-panel detector uses a scintillator that changes x-rays into light. The scintillator is
explanation: Cesium iodide or gadolinium oxysulfide emits light, which a photodetector then converts to an electric signal.

stem: On a digital display, changing the window level changes the image's
explanation: Window level sets brightness; window width sets contrast.

stem: On a digital display, narrowing the window width
explanation: A narrower window spreads fewer gray values across the display, so contrast increases.

stem: A grainy, freckled appearance (quantum mottle) in an image is most often caused by
options: too few photons, such as too little mAs
explanation: Quantum noise appears when too few photons reach the receptor, usually from insufficient mAs.

stem: In a digital image, spatial resolution improves as
explanation: Smaller pixels show finer detail; for the same field of view, a larger matrix means smaller pixels.

stem: For the same field of view, increasing the matrix size gives
options: smaller pixels and better spatial resolution
explanation: More pixels across the same field means each pixel is smaller, so detail improves.

stem: Compared with film-screen imaging, CR and DR systems have
explanation: Digital receptors respond over a much wider range of exposures, which gives them a wide dynamic range and exposure latitude.

stem: Digital systems display an exposure indicator mainly to
options: help avoid dose creep by showing the exposure that reached the receptor
explanation: Because software corrects image brightness, overexposure is not visible; the exposure indicator (S number, EI or REX, by manufacturer) shows it and helps prevent dose creep.

stem: In a digital system, the device that changes the detector's analog signal into digital data is the
explanation: The analog-to-digital converter (ADC) turns the electric signal from the detector into numbers the computer can process.

stem: The system that stores digital images and distributes them for viewing is the
explanation: A picture archiving and communication system (PACS) stores, retrieves and displays images across the facility.

stem: The best way to reduce blur from involuntary motion, such as peristalsis, is to use
explanation: Involuntary motion cannot be stopped by instructions, so a short exposure time is the main defense.

stem: Increasing the SID, with the technique adjusted, will
options: decrease magnification and improve recorded detail
explanation: A longer SID makes the beam less divergent, which reduces magnification and unsharpness.

stem: Which condition generally requires an increase in exposure factors?
explanation: Ascites adds fluid to the abdomen, making it harder to penetrate (an additive condition). The other three make tissue easier to penetrate.

stem: Which condition generally requires a decrease in exposure factors?
explanation: Osteoporosis reduces bone density (a destructive condition), so less exposure is needed.

stem: Collimators that automatically adjust the field to the size of the image receptor are called
explanation: Positive beam limitation (PBL) senses the receptor size and collimates the beam to it.
